name: Neo-brutalism
basis: web design style: flat bands, thick black outlines, offset hard shadow (how)

lumenary.blurb: Flat colour blocks, thick black outlines and a hard offset shadow.

facts.bestOn: Punchy subjects with strong shapes, such as products and portraits

why: Neo-brutalism borrows the honesty of raw concrete architecture: nothing is hidden, nothing is blurred. Thick black outlines, flat colour and a shadow that is simply a second black rectangle make the picture look like a sticker pressed onto a page. It is loud on purpose, and it stays readable at any size.
how: Crop the picture to fill a window, keeping the centre.
Blur it a little and measure brightness.
Cut the brightness into a few equal bands and give each band one flat colour.
Find edges and draw them as thick black outlines.
Draw a black rectangle offset behind the card as the hard shadow, then add the optional title bar.
history: The name comes from brutalism, the mid twentieth century architecture of exposed concrete (from the French béton brut, raw concrete). Brutalist web design appeared in the mid 2010s as a reaction to polished, identical templates. Neo-brutalism softened it with bright colours and friendly shapes and became a popular look for apps and landing pages in the early 2020s.
uses: Landing pages and app interface kits
Social posts that need to stand out in a feed
terms: A shadow with no blur, drawn as a solid offset copy of the shape.
To reduce a picture to a few flat tones.
An architectural style of raw, unfinished concrete surfaces.
paragraphs: Neo-brutalism is flat colour, thick black borders and shadows that do not blur. The picture is first cropped to fill a window (the larger of the width and height ratios decides the scale, and the centre is kept), then blurred and measured for brightness. The brightness range is cut into n equal bands and each band is given one colour from a bright palette, so the picture becomes a poster of flat colour regions, with colours spread evenly through the palette.

Black outlines come from Sobel again, here with a harder smoothstep so lines are crisp, and a heavier weight meaning a wider neighbourhood. The card sits on a plain coloured background, with a black rectangle of the same size drawn offset by the shadow distance, with no blur at all, which is the whole of the “hard shadow”. A title bar with three flat squares and a title, drawn in the same black as the borders, is optional chrome. Border width and shadow offset are tied to the picture width, so the look is the same at any export size.

equations.note: Pick one of m palette colours P for each of n brightness bands.
Cover-crop of the picture into a w × h window.

presets.text: Fewer colour blocks and heavier lines give a poster feel.
Candy colours on a pink backdrop read as playful rather than harsh.
Push the shadow to the maximum for a very dimensional card.
